title: Constraining Primordial Power Asymmetry from Galaxy Clustering and Peculiar Velocity Information
summary: Primordial power asymmetry would probe departures from statistical isotropy, offering a clue to the physics of the primordial Universe. We investigate how such asymmetries can be tested with galaxy surveys and quantify how peculiar-velocity information can improve these tests. We develop a unified bipolar spherical harmonic (BipoSH) analysis of the auto- and cross-power spectra of galaxy density and line-of-sight peculiar velocity, and perform Fisher forecasts combining a Euclid-like spectroscopic galaxy survey with peculiar velocities reconstructed from Simons Observatory-like CMB maps through the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect. For dipolar asymmetry, we consider both scale-independent and scale-dependent modulations proportional to $k^{-0.5}$. Galaxy clustering provides most of the constraining power in both cases, while peculiar velocities add only modest information. For quadrupolar asymmetry, we account for the recently identified anisotropic galaxy-bias response and marginalize over its amplitude. We find that galaxy clustering alone suffers from a degeneracy between the primordial quadrupolar modulation and anisotropic galaxy bias. This degeneracy can be substantially broken by adding peculiar-velocity information: the density-velocity cross-spectrum provides complementary information to the galaxy auto-spectrum, while the velocity auto-spectrum constrains the primordial modulation independently of anisotropic galaxy bias. The velocity information becomes increasingly effective for more negative scale dependence, yielding constraints tighter than those from BOSS for scale dependences proportional to $k^{-1}$ and $k^{-2}$. Our results demonstrate that peculiar-velocity information provides a complementary avenue for testing primordial power asymmetry with large-scale structure, particularly for quadrupolar asymmetry in the presence of anisotropic galaxy bias.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how primordial power asymmetry can be tested with galaxy surveys, developing a unified bipolar spherical harmonic (BipoSH) analysis of galaxy density and line-of-sight peculiar velocity power spectra. Using Fisher forecasts combining Euclid-like spectroscopic surveys with Simons Observatory-like CMB-derived peculiar velocities, the authors find that galaxy clustering dominates dipolar asymmetry constraints, while peculiar velocities substantially break degeneracies for quadrupolar asymmetry—particularly the degeneracy between primordial quadrupolar modulation and anisotropic galaxy bias.
AI.motivation: Primordial power asymmetry would probe departures from statistical isotropy, offering clues to physics of the primordial Universe. The authors aim to quantify how peculiar-velocity information can improve tests of such asymmetries with galaxy surveys.
AI.method: The authors develop a unified bipolar spherical harmonic (BipoSH) analysis of auto- and cross-power spectra of galaxy density and line-of-sight peculiar velocity. They perform Fisher forecasts combining a Euclid-like spectroscopic galaxy survey with peculiar velocities reconstructed from Simons Observatory-like CMB maps via the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect. They consider both scale-independent and scale-dependent dipolar modulations (proportional to k^-0.5), and for quadrupolar asymmetry they account for and marginalize over the anisotropic galaxy-bias response.
AI.result: For dipolar asymmetry, galaxy clustering provides most constraining power, with peculiar velocities adding only modest information. For quadrupolar asymmetry, galaxy clustering alone suffers from a degeneracy between primordial quadrupolar modulation and anisotropic galaxy bias, which is substantially broken by adding peculiar-velocity information. The density-velocity cross-spectrum provides complementary information, while the velocity auto-spectrum constrains the primordial modulation independently of anisotropic galaxy bias. Velocity information becomes increasingly effective for more negative scale dependence, yielding tighter constraints than BOSS for scale dependences proportional to k^-1 and k^-2.
AI.conclusion: Peculiar-velocity information provides a complementary avenue for testing primordial power asymmetry with large-scale structure, particularly for quadrupolar asymmetry where it breaks degeneracies with anisotropic galaxy bias.

title: Cosmographic Reconstruction of the Quintessence Potential in Scalar-Tensor Gravity
comment: 25 pages, 5 figures. The numerical analysis files used for the reproduction of the figures can be found at: https://github.com/leandros11/st-reconstruction
summary: We generalise the cosmographic reconstruction programme of Chakraborty, Dunsby & Scherrer to scalar-tensor gravity. Working in the Jordan frame with a general non-minimal coupling $F(Φ)$, we derive exact closed-form expressions for the potential slope $λ_U$, the coupling slope $λ_F$, and their curvature parameters $Γ_U$ and $Γ_F$ in terms of the cosmographic parameters $(q,j,s)$, the Planck-mass running $α_M = d\ln F/d\ln a$ and its derivatives. We express $α_M$ and its derivatives in terms of a set of coefficients $g_n$ describing the time variation of the gravitational constant $G\propto F^{-1}$, casting all four quantities in fully observable form. We then evaluate the reconstruction against current data, including DESI~DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation measurements and Lunar Laser Ranging constraints on $\dot G/G$, propagating the cosmographic uncertainties through to the reconstructed potential. All expressions reduce analytically to those of Chakraborty, Dunsby & Scherrer in the minimally-coupled limit, which we verify symbolically. We find that the potential slope $λ_U$ is recovered at the few-tenths level while the curvature $Γ_U$ is essentially unconstrained. We further show that the positivity of the scalar kinetic term is equivalent to $w_{\rm eff,0}\ge-1$, so that the region of cosmographic parameter space closed to minimally-coupled quintessence is exactly the phantom region, and that the non-minimal coupling reopens it through a single coefficient $g_2$ of the gravitational tower. Because Lunar Laser Ranging forces $|g_1|\lesssim2\times10^{-4}$ while the reconstruction is sensitive to $g_2\sim O(0.1)$, the framework presupposes that $α_M$ is passing through zero at the present epoch, as expected on the Damour--Nordtvedt least-coupling attractor.

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes the cosmographic reconstruction programme from minimally-coupled to scalar-tensor gravity, deriving exact closed-form expressions for the potential slope λ_U, coupling slope λ_F, and their curvature parameters Γ_U and Γ_F in terms of cosmographic quantities (q,j,s), the Planck-mass running α_M, and its derivatives. The framework is evaluated against DESI DR2 BAO and Lunar Laser Ranging data, showing λ_U is recovered at the few-tenths level while Γ_U is unconstrained. Key findings: the scalar kinetic term positivity constraint is equivalent to w_eff,0 ≥ −1 (phantom region), non-minimal coupling reopens the cosmographic parameter space through a single coefficient g_2, and Lunar Laser Ranging constraints imply α_M passes through zero at present epoch as expected by the Damour–Nordtvedt attractor.
AI.motivation: To extend the cosmographic reconstruction programme—previously developed for minimally-coupled quintessence—to general scalar-tensor gravity in the Jordan frame, enabling a fully observable reconstruction of the scalar-tensor potential and coupling without assuming a specific model a priori.
AI.method: Working in the Jordan frame with general non-minimal coupling F(Φ), the authors derive exact closed-form expressions for λ_U, λ_F, Γ_U, Γ_F in terms of cosmographic parameters (q,j,s), the Planck-mass running α_M = d ln F/d ln a, and its derivatives. These are recast in fully observable form using coefficients g_n describing G ∝ F^{−1} time variation. The reconstruction is then tested against DESI DR2 BAO data and Lunar Laser Ranging constraints on Ġ/G, with cosmographic uncertainties propagated to the reconstructed potential. Symbolic verification confirms analytic reduction to the minimally-coupled limit.
AI.result: The potential slope λ_U is recovered at the few-tenths precision level while Γ_U is essentially unconstrained by current data. The positivity of the scalar kinetic term is shown to be equivalent to w_eff,0 ≥ −1, meaning the cosmographic region closed to minimally-coupled quintessence is exactly the phantom region; the non-minimal coupling reopens this region through a single coefficient g_2. Lunar Laser Ranging forces |g_1| ≲ 2×10^{-4} while reconstruction is sensitive to g_2 ∼ O(0.1), implying α_M passes through zero at the present epoch, consistent with the Damour–Nordtvedt least-coupling attractor.
AI.conclusion: The cosmographic reconstruction programme is successfully generalised to scalar-tensor gravity in fully observable form. While λ_U is well constrained, Γ_U remains effectively unobservable with current data. The non-minimal coupling provides a natural mechanism—mediated by g_2—to reopen the phantom region that is forbidden for minimally-coupled quintessence, and current gravitational constraints imply α_M is near zero today, consistent with the Damour–Nordtvedt least-coupling attractor.

title: Cosmicflows-4 and the Cosmological Consistency of Large-Scale Motions
summary: We study coherent flows in Cosmicflows-4 (CF4) and its constituent catalogs. We fit monopole and dipole moments in nonoverlapping radial bins using a log-distance radial-velocity estimator. For each sample, the Planck 2018 $Λ$CDM prediction accounts for the actual positions, statistical weights, velocity covariance, and measurement covariance. Across six bins extending to $300,h^{-1},\mathrm{Mpc}$, the All Individual sample is broadly consistent with $Λ$CDM, with dipole and joint deviations of $2.29σ$ and $2.36σ$. The strongest localized feature occurs at $120$--$160,h^{-1},\mathrm{Mpc}$, where $|V_{\rm dip}|=628\pm82,\mathrm{km,s^{-1}}$ and the dipole deviation reaches $3.40σ$. The excess is concentrated toward negative supergalactic X and depends strongly on the survey window. TFR and 6dFGS favor larger dipoles, while SDSS and SN favor smaller ones. Removing 6dFGS reduces the upper-bin dipole deviation to $1.56σ$, while removing SN raises it to $3.77σ$. Nevertheless, the SN and 6dFGS dipoles remain mutually consistent when their covariance is included. SDSS is consistent with $Λ$CDM through $160,h^{-1},\mathrm{Mpc}$ but shows a separate rise at larger radii whose significance depends on the treatment of the monopole and shared distance-scale covariance. Overall, CF4 does not show uniformly anomalous motion across its full radial range. Instead, it contains localized and window-dependent features that should be tested with selection-matched mock catalogs and correlated calibration uncertainties.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes coherent flows in the Cosmicflows-4 catalog, fitting monopole and dipole moments in radial bins and comparing them against Planck 2018 ΛCDM predictions. While the full sample is broadly consistent with ΛCDM (deviations ~2.3σ), a localized dipole excess at 120-160 h⁻¹Mpc reaches 3.40σ significance, concentrated toward negative supergalactic X. The excess is highly sensitive to survey window and specific subsamples (TFR, 6dFGS vs SDSS, SN), with CF4 showing localized, window-dependent features rather than uniformly anomalous motion.
AI.motivation: To determine whether Cosmicflows-4 reveals coherent (bulk) flows that are anomalous compared to the standard ΛCDM model, and to characterize the radial structure and survey-window dependence of any detected dipole deviations, since previous bulk-flow analyses have shown conflicting results across different catalogs and distance indicators.
AI.method: The authors fit monopole and dipole velocity moments in six nonoverlapping radial bins extending to 300 h⁻¹Mpc using a log-distance radial-velocity estimator. Each sample is compared against the Planck 2018 ΛCDM prediction, accounting for actual galaxy positions, statistical weights, velocity covariance, and measurement covariance. The analysis is performed on CF4 and its constituent catalogs (TFR, 6dFGS, SDSS, SN) separately, including sensitivity tests where individual subsamples are removed.
AI.result: The All Individual CF4 sample is broadly consistent with ΛCDM (dipole deviation 2.29σ, joint 2.36σ), but shows a localized 3.40σ dipole excess at 120-160 h⁻¹Mpc with |V_dip|=628±82 km/s, concentrated toward negative supergalactic X. TFR and 6dFGS favor larger dipoles while SDSS and SN favor smaller ones. Removing 6dFGS reduces the upper-bin deviation to 1.56σ; removing SN raises it to 3.77σ, though SN and 6dFGS dipoles remain mutually consistent with covariance. SDSS is consistent with ΛCDM through 160 h⁻¹Mpc but shows a separate rise at larger radii whose significance depends on monopole treatment and shared distance-scale covariance.
AI.conclusion: CF4 does not exhibit uniformly anomalous bulk flow across its full radial range. Instead, it contains localized and window-dependent features, particularly a 3.4σ excess at 120-160 h⁻¹Mpc. These features should be further tested against selection-matched mock catalogs and with correlated calibration uncertainties properly modeled before claiming a genuine tension with ΛCDM.

title: How X-rays heat the IGM in different 21-cm simulation codes: a comparison between Licorice and Beorn
summary: Any interpretation of the 21-cm signal of neutral hydrogen using Bayesian inference methods can only be as accurate as the underlying simulation code used to model the state of the intergalactic medium (IGM). 3D radiative transfer (RT) simulation codes may capture complex physics, but are computationally expensive and, therefore, faster, more approximate codes have been developed. To improve our understanding of the convergence of simulation codes in the 21-cm science community, we present a comparison of the X-ray heating of the IGM modelled in Licorice, a 3D RT simulation code, and Beorn, a 1D RT code. We use Beorn to process sources extracted from Licorice simulations, using the same physics of the sources, in order to obtain two versions of the temperature of the IGM heated by X-rays. We observe a good agreement between the luminosity fields, mean temperatures, and global 21-cm signal of the two setups, but discrepancies in the distribution of temperature and 21-cm signal, which result in a $\sim 30\%$ difference in the 21-cm power spectrum. We attempt to isolate the approximations that lead to these differences and find that common approximations used in 1D RT codes produce effects of that magnitude. Using an emulator of the Licorice power spectra in an MCMC pipeline, we translate these differences between power spectra into differences between posterior distributions over the astrophysical parameters. We observe a typical bias between 1D posteriors of $\gtrsim 1 σ$ (with a noise level corresponding to 100h of SKA observations).

AI.tldr: This paper compares two radiative transfer simulation codes—Licorice (3D RT) and Beorn (1D RT)—for modeling X-ray heating of the intergalactic medium in 21-cm signal studies. While they agree on luminosity fields, mean temperatures, and global 21-cm signal, discrepancies in temperature distribution and power spectra (~30% difference) arise from common 1D RT approximations. These propagate through MCMC-based Bayesian inference, biasing posterior distributions of astrophysical parameters by ≳1σ at SKA noise levels.
AI.motivation: Bayesian inference of the 21-cm signal relies on simulation codes whose accuracy limits the validity of inferred astrophysical parameters. While 3D RT codes capture complex physics, they are computationally prohibitive, leading to the wide use of faster 1D codes. Understanding the convergence and discrepancies between these code classes is essential for reliable interpretation of upcoming 21-cm observations.
AI.method: The authors run Licorice (3D RT) simulations and use Beorn (1D RT) to process the same source catalogs extracted from Licorice with identical source physics. They compare luminosity fields, mean temperature, global 21-cm signal, temperature distributions, and 21-cm power spectra between the two setups. They then use an emulator of Licorice power spectra within an MCMC pipeline to translate power-spectrum differences into posterior differences over astrophysical parameters.
AI.result: The codes agree on luminosity fields, mean temperatures, and the global 21-cm signal, but differ in the distribution of temperature and 21-cm signal, producing ~30% differences in the 21-cm power spectrum. These differences are attributable to common approximations in 1D RT codes. In an MCMC analysis at SKA noise levels (100h), the resulting posterior bias between 1D codes is ≳1 standard deviation.
AI.conclusion: Common approximations in fast 1D RT codes introduce systematic differences in 21-cm power spectra and can bias inferred astrophysical parameters at a level exceeding 1σ for SKA-like observations. This highlights the need for careful code validation and calibration when using approximate simulations for Bayesian inference of the 21-cm signal.

title: Orbital Migration of Interacting Stellar Mass Black Holes in Disks around Supermassive Black Holes. III. Mass Distribution of Hierarchical Mergers
summary: Active galactic nucleus (AGN) disks are a promising location for the formation of binary black holes (BBHs) that will merge on relatively short timescales and be detected by LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK). To compare the mass function (MF) of black holes (BHs) undergoing hierarchical mergers in AGN disks to the inferred MFs from LVK observations, we perform 360 simulations with an N-body code augmented to include an analytic model for migration torques and other gas forces. We focus on the region surrounding migration traps in AGN disks where migration torques cancel out and BHs converge. We find that regardless of changes in the initial MF and BBH merger criteria, frequent mergers deplete the number of BHs with masses $\lesssim 10$~$M_\odot$ and fill the upper mass gap with a roughly uniform distribution from 40--100~$M_\odot$, with a slight overabundance around ${\approx}70~M_\odot$ from resonant orbiters. We also find an average merger rate of $\sim 6$~Gpc$^{-3}$~yr$^{-1}$ for migration-trap-aided BBH mergers in our AGN disk model. $\sim 40\%$ of these mergers have uneven mass ratios and 16\% have a primary mass $\in[50-100]~M_\odot$. Therefore, AGN disks could easily be the source of BBH mergers observed by LVK that are difficult to produce through traditional stellar evolution channels. Our simulations also form a separate higher-mass intermediate mass black hole (IMBH) population $>200~M_\odot$ after $\sim 2$~Myr. Future gravitational wave detectors can use observations of this IMBH population to constrain models of AGN accretion disks.

AI.tldr: This paper presents 360 N-body simulations of hierarchical binary black hole (BBH) mergers in AGN disks, augmented with analytic migration torques and gas forces, focusing on migration traps where BHs converge. The simulations show that frequent mergers deplete BHs with masses below ~10 M☉, produce a roughly uniform distribution in the upper mass gap (40-100 M☉) with a slight overabundance around 70 M☉, yield an average merger rate of ~6 Gpc⁻³ yr⁻¹ (with ~40% uneven mass ratios and 16% with primary mass in 50-100 M☉), and form a separate intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) population >200 M☉ after ~2 Myr.
AI.motivation: To determine whether AGN disks can produce binary black hole mergers with mass functions consistent with LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) observations, particularly for mergers that are difficult to produce through traditional stellar evolution channels, and to constrain AGN disk models using gravitational wave detections.
AI.method: The authors perform 360 simulations using an N-body code augmented with an analytic model for migration torques and other gas forces. They focus on the migration trap region in AGN disks where migration torques cancel and BHs converge, testing variations in the initial mass function and BBH merger criteria.
AI.result: Frequent mergers deplete BHs below ~10 M☉ and fill the upper mass gap with a roughly uniform distribution from 40-100 M☉, with a slight overabundance near 70 M☉ from resonant orbiters. The average merger rate is ~6 Gpc⁻³ yr⁻¹, with ~40% having uneven mass ratios and 16% having primary masses in [50-100] M☉. A separate IMBH population >200 M☉ forms after ~2 Myr.
AI.conclusion: AGN disks could easily be the source of BBH mergers observed by LVK that are difficult to produce through traditional stellar evolution channels. Observations of the distinct IMBH population by future gravitational wave detectors can be used to constrain models of AGN accretion disks.

title: Abundant Heavy Black Hole Seeds from Moderate Lyman-Werner Radiation
summary: The existence of high-redshift quasars may indicate that massive black hole seeds formed via supermassive Population III stars in atomic-cooling halos with large gas inflow rates; however, the dependence of this process on halo assembly rate and radiative background remains poorly constrained. We present a large suite of 65 high-resolution cosmological zoom-in simulations of 15 pristine halos spanning a wide range of Lyman-Werner radiation backgrounds and halo assembly histories. We introduce a novel method to estimate the final Population III stellar mass from radial gas infall profiles at the onset of runaway collapse and validate it against simulations from the literature that explicitly follow protostellar accretion with sink particles, reproducing protostellar masses to within a factor of $\sim2$. We find a clear transition in gas inflow rates between halos exposed to $J_{\rm 21} \lesssim 1$ and $J_{\rm 21} \gtrsim 10$, with the latter frequently sustaining inflow rates above the adopted threshold for supermassive star formation and producing estimated stellar masses up to $10^{5} \, M_{\odot}$. In contrast, the halo assembly timescale, $M_{\rm Halo}$/$\dot{M}_{\rm Halo}$, shows no statistically significant correlation with predicted stellar mass, despite halo assembly rates spanning $0.01$-$7 \, M_{\rm \odot} \, {\rm yr}^{-1}$. The Lyman-Werner radiation field therefore is a stronger predictor of sustained high accretion within our parameter space. Finally, a semi-analytic model applied to cosmological volumes shows that halos exposed to intermediate Lyman-Werner backgrounds ($1 \lesssim J_{\rm 21} < 10$) are orders of magnitude more common than those in the high-$J_{\rm 21}$ tail. If sustained high accretion extends into this intermediate regime, heavy black hole seeds may form in substantially more common environments than required by classical direct-collapse scenarios.

AI.tldr: This paper uses 65 high-resolution cosmological zoom-in simulations of 15 pristine halos to study how Lyman-Werner radiation backgrounds and halo assembly rates affect massive black hole seed formation via supermassive Population III stars. They find a clear transition in gas inflow rates between halos with J21 ≲ 1 and J21 ≳ 10, with the latter producing stellar masses up to 10^5 M⊙, while halo assembly timescale shows no significant correlation. A semi-analytic model suggests intermediate Lyman-Werner backgrounds (1 ≲ J21 < 10) may host heavy black hole seed formation in substantially more common environments than previously thought.
AI.motivation: To constrain the dependence of supermassive Population III star formation (and thus massive black hole seed formation) on halo assembly rate and Lyman-Werner radiative background, which remains poorly understood despite high-redshift quasar observations suggesting such massive seeds exist.
AI.method: A suite of 65 high-resolution cosmological zoom-in simulations of 15 pristine halos, varying Lyman-Werner radiation backgrounds and spanning diverse halo assembly histories. A novel method estimates final Population III stellar mass from radial gas infall profiles at the onset of runaway collapse, validated against sink-particle simulations from the literature. A semi-analytic model is also applied to cosmological volumes to assess the abundance of halos in different Lyman-Werner background regimes.
AI.result: A clear transition in gas inflow rates occurs between halos exposed to J21 ≲ 1 and J21 ≳ 10, with the latter frequently sustaining inflow rates above the supermassive star formation threshold and producing stellar masses up to 10^5 M⊙. Halo assembly timescale shows no statistically significant correlation with predicted stellar mass despite assembly rates spanning 0.01-7 M⊙ yr^-1. Halos at intermediate Lyman-Werner backgrounds (1 ≲ J21 < 10) are orders of magnitude more common than those in the high-J21 tail.
AI.conclusion: The Lyman-Werner radiation field is a stronger predictor of sustained high accretion than halo assembly rate within the probed parameter space. If sustained high accretion extends into the intermediate Lyman-Werner regime (1 ≲ J21 < 10), heavy black hole seeds could form in significantly more common environments than required by classical direct-collapse scenarios.

title: Old Disks Die Hard: How Does AGN Feedback Suppress Disk Formation in Milky Way Mass Galaxies?
summary: The connection between a galaxy's visual shape and its star formation rate is one of the oldest established trends in galaxy evolution, yet the origin of this trend remains unsettled. We analyze two Milky-Way mass halos simulated with FIRE-2 galaxy formation physics, each run without AGN and with up to three implementations of AGN feedback. We use them to study how and why AGN star formation suppression affects morphological evolution over cosmic time. Both runs without AGN feedback produce prominent, thin, star-forming spiral disks at $z=0$. Each of the AGN runs has less late-time star formation, and ends up with a higher spheroid fraction and a lower thin-disk mass fraction. In two instances, the AGN runs produce quenched lenticular galaxies with no cool gas at $z=0$. The main reason for these morphological differences is that AGN feedback becomes effective {\em just after} the onset of disk formation, at ``spin up," in every run. This time-differentiated impact suppresses the formation of disk stars, especially thin-disk stars, preferentially because thin-disk formation occurs late. The spheroidal components are assembled early in all runs, before AGN feedback is effective, and are therefore similar in mass and size across runs.

AI.tldr: Using FIRE-2 simulations of two Milky-Way mass halos run without AGN and with up to three AGN feedback implementations, the authors show that AGN feedback suppresses late-time star formation, yielding higher spheroid fractions and lower thin-disk mass fractions, sometimes producing quenched lenticular galaxies. The key mechanism is that AGN feedback becomes effective just after disk formation begins ("spin up"), preferentially suppressing late-forming thin-disk stars while leaving early-assembled spheroids largely unaffected.
AI.motivation: The connection between a galaxy's visual morphology and its star formation rate is a long-established but mechanistically unexplained trend. The authors aim to understand how and why AGN-driven star formation suppression affects morphological evolution over cosmic time.
AI.method: Analysis of two Milky-Way mass halos simulated with FIRE-2 galaxy formation physics, each run without AGN and with up to three implementations of AGN feedback. Morphological evolution is compared across runs at z=0, including spheroid fraction, thin-disk mass fraction, cool gas content, and quenching status.
AI.result: All non-AGN runs produce prominent, thin, star-forming spiral disks at z=0, while AGN runs show reduced late-time star formation with higher spheroid fractions and lower thin-disk mass fractions. Two AGN runs produce quenched lenticular galaxies with no cool gas. The morphological differences arise because AGN feedback becomes effective just after disk formation onset ("spin up"), preferentially suppressing late-forming thin-disk stars while early-assembled spheroids remain similar in mass and size across all runs.
AI.conclusion: The origin of the morphology-star formation trend lies in the time-differentiated impact of AGN feedback: because thin-disk formation occurs late and AGN becomes effective right after disk onset, AGN preferentially suppresses thin-disk star formation, inflating spheroid fractions and quenching galaxies. Spheroids assembled before AGN activation are immune to this effect.

title: The CMZ Asymmetries: Feeding or Feedback?
summary: Three-fourths of the dense gas and dust in the CMZ is located at positive longitudes and positive radial velocities. The majority of compact 24 micrometer wavelength sources are at negative longitudes. These two asymmetries indicate either a recent asymmetric injection of gas along the bar dust lanes, or that most of the molecular gas is contained in a small number of massive, gravitationally bound clouds, or a major feedback episode which dissociated an entire sector of the CMZ's dense gas.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes asymmetries in the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ): most dense gas and dust is at positive longitudes and radial velocities, while most compact 24 μm sources are at negative longitudes, suggesting asymmetric gas injection, massive bound clouds, or major feedback dissociation.
AI.motivation: To understand the physical processes driving the observed asymmetries in the distribution of dense gas and dust versus compact infrared sources in the Central Molecular Zone of the Milky Way.
AI.method: The study compares the spatial distribution of dense gas and dust (at positive longitudes and radial velocities) against compact 24 μm sources (at negative longitudes) to identify asymmetries and infer their causes.
AI.result: Three-fourths of the dense gas and dust in the CMZ is found at positive longitudes and positive radial velocities, while the majority of compact 24 μm sources are located at negative longitudes, revealing a clear spatial asymmetry between these tracers.
AI.conclusion: The observed asymmetry indicates one of three possible origins: recent asymmetric injection of gas along the bar dust lanes, concentration of most molecular gas in a small number of massive gravitationally bound clouds, or a major feedback episode that dissociated a whole sector of the CMZ's dense gas.

title: Energy Partitioning in Dust-catalyzed $\mathrm{H_2}$ and HD Formation Revealed by Molecular Simulations Considering Nuclear Quantum Effects
summary: Molecular hydrogen formation on interstellar dust grains is a key surface process in the interstellar medium, but the redistribution of the recombination energy between the substrate and the nascent molecule remains poorly understood. Here, we use ring-polymer molecular dynamics (RPMD) with a machine-learning force field to investigate energy partitioning during $\mathrm{H_2}$ and $\mathrm{HD}$ formation on graphene at $T=25, 50$ and $100 \mathrm{K}$. We focus on the chemisorbed-H recombination pathway previously identified as the dominant low-temperature channel on bare graphitic surfaces when nuclear quantum effects are included. The desorbing molecule retains the major fraction of the effective surface-mediated released energy, while graphene absorbs a smaller but non-negligible part. This molecular retention fraction is nearly temperature-independent over the investigated range. In contrast, the post-formation molecular kinetic-energy distribution changes more strongly with temperature: rovibrational motion dominates at low temperature, whereas center-of-mass translation becomes increasingly important at $100 \mathrm{K}$. $\mathrm{H_2}$ and $\mathrm{HD}$ exhibit broadly similar total energy retention, with only modest isotope-dependent differences in their internal kinetic-energy partitioning. These results provide an energy-resolved microscopic picture of surface-mediated energy redistribution in $\mathrm{H_2}$/$\mathrm{HD}$ formation, with implications for formation-pumping signatures in high-excitation $\mathrm{H_2}$ lines, vibrationally excited $\mathrm{H_2}$ chemistry, and collisional excitation of coexisting molecules by translationally hot nascent $\mathrm{H_2}$ in cold interstellar gas.

AI.tldr: This study uses ring-polymer molecular dynamics with a machine-learning force field to examine energy partitioning during H2 and HD formation on graphene at 25, 50, and 100 K. The desorbing molecule retains most of the released energy, which is nearly temperature-independent, while the graphene substrate absorbs a smaller but non-negligible fraction. Temperature affects the energy distribution mode: rovibrational motion dominates at low T, while translational motion gains importance at 100 K. Only modest isotope-dependent differences exist between H2 and HD, providing an energy-resolved microscopic picture with implications for interstellar H2 formation-pumping signatures.
AI.motivation: Understanding how the recombination energy is redistributed between the substrate and the nascent H2 molecule during molecular hydrogen formation on interstellar dust grains is poorly understood, yet it is critical for interpreting H2 line emissions and interstellar chemistry.
AI.method: Ring-polymer molecular dynamics (RPMD) simulations with a machine-learning force field were employed to study the chemisorbed-H recombination pathway on graphene at temperatures of 25, 50, and 100 K, including nuclear quantum effects.
AI.result: The desorbing H2/HD molecule retains the majority of the surface-mediated released energy, nearly independent of temperature, while graphene absorbs a smaller but non-negligible portion. The internal kinetic-energy distribution changes with temperature: rovibrational motion dominates at low T, while translational motion becomes increasingly significant at 100 K. H2 and HD show broadly similar total energy retention with only modest isotope-dependent partitioning differences.
AI.conclusion: The work provides an energy-resolved microscopic picture of energy partitioning in surface-mediated H2 and HD formation, with implications for formation-pumping signatures in high-excitation H2 lines, vibrationally excited H2 chemistry, and collisional excitation of coexisting molecules in cold interstellar gas.

title: How mergers shape galaxy morphology in the IllustrisTNG simulation
summary: How galaxy mergers drive morphological evolution remains an open question. Traditional views hold that major mergers produce elliptical galaxies, while minor mergers form dispersion-dominated components such as galactic bulges. However, more recent work has challenged this simple picture, suggesting a more complex evolutionary scenario. In this study, we use the IllustrisTNG cosmological simulation to investigate how mergers shape galaxy morphology, across a broad range of galaxy masses and merger mass ratios. Our results show that the post-merger galaxy morphology is primarily determined by three factors: collision angle $\overlineθ$, cold gas fraction $f_\mathrm{cold\,gas}$, and pre-merger galaxy morphology $\mathrm{(B/T)_{*,pre}}$. Specifically, spiral-in mergers with large $\overlineθ$ increase the rotational support of the system, allowing the gas to settle into an extended disk. When the system is rich in cold gas, star formation within the newly formed gas disk can further strengthen the disk-dominated structure of the remnant. On the other hand, head-on mergers with small $\overlineθ$ typically disrupt ordered galactic motion, producing more dispersion-supported remnants. Overall, we interpret our results within a unified picture of merger-driven morphological transformation in galaxies.

AI.tldr: Using the IllustrisTNG cosmological simulation, this study investigates how galaxy mergers drive morphological evolution, finding that post-merger morphology is primarily determined by collision angle, cold gas fraction, and pre-merger morphology. Spiral-in mergers with large collision angles and abundant cold gas produce disk-dominated remnants, while head-on mergers produce dispersion-supported systems.
AI.motivation: Traditional views hold that major mergers produce ellipticals and minor mergers form bulges, but recent work challenges this simple picture. The open question of how galaxy mergers drive morphological evolution motivates a more systematic investigation using cosmological simulations across a broad range of galaxy masses and merger mass ratios.
AI.method: The study uses the IllustrisTNG cosmological simulation to investigate merger-driven morphological transformation across a wide range of galaxy masses and merger mass ratios, analyzing how three key factors (collision angle, cold gas fraction, and pre-merger morphology) determine post-merger morphology.
AI.result: Post-merger morphology is primarily determined by collision angle, cold gas fraction, and pre-merger morphology. Spiral-in mergers with large collision angles enhance rotational support and enable gas to settle into extended disks, where star formation further strengthens disk dominance. Head-on mergers with small collision angles disrupt ordered motion and produce dispersion-supported remnants.
AI.conclusion: The results support a unified picture of merger-driven morphological transformation, where the outcome depends on the interplay between the merger geometry, gas content, and the initial galaxy structure, rather than a simple dichotomy based on merger mass ratio alone.

title: The SAMI Galaxy Survey: Linking Tidal Features and Orbit Populations Using Schwarzschild Modelling
comment: 32 pages, 25 figures, accepted to Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society (MNRAS)
summary: The evolution of angular momentum in galaxies is shaped by a combination of internal secular processes and external mechanisms such as mergers. Orbit-superposition based dynamical modelling provides a powerful means of linking the intrinsic orbital structures of galaxies to their global properties and merger histories. We construct Schwarzschild orbit-superposition models of massive ($\log(M/M_{\odot})>10$) SAMI galaxies using the DYNAMITE code, utilising deep KiDS photometry to accurately reproduce each galaxy's luminosity distribution. We find that the fractions of hot, cold, warm, and counter-rotating orbits all show significant correlations with the spin parameter proxy $λ_{R_e}$, with the strongest correlation arising from the combined hot plus counter-rotating fraction. When controlling for stellar mass and environment, we find that the fraction of hot and cold orbits show significant correlations with stellar age, whereas warm orbits do not. We further find that the lower values of $λ_{R_e}$ for young galaxies with shell merger features as compared to the full sample is driven by an excess of hot orbits and a deficit of cold orbits, with no dependence on warm orbits. We suggest that the kinematic transformation in this SAMI sample proceeds through stars transitioning directly from cold to hot orbits. As warm orbits are expected to arise from secular heating processes, these findings indicate that merger-driven heating is the dominant mechanism governing the redistribution of angular momentum and the reduction of rotational support in massive galaxies.

AI.tldr: Using Schwarzschild orbit-superposition dynamical models of massive SAMI galaxies with the DYNAMITE code and deep KiDS photometry, the study finds that orbital fractions (hot, cold, warm, counter-rotating) correlate with the spin parameter λ_Re, with the strongest correlation from combined hot plus counter-rotating fraction. Hot and cold orbit fractions correlate with stellar age (controlling for mass and environment), and the reduced λ_Re in young galaxies with merger shells is driven by excess hot and deficit cold orbits. The results suggest kinematic transformation proceeds via direct cold-to-hot orbital transitions, indicating merger-driven heating dominates angular momentum redistribution in massive galaxies.
AI.motivation: To understand how angular momentum evolves in galaxies by linking intrinsic orbital structures to global properties and merger histories, using orbit-superposition dynamical modelling.
AI.method: Constructed Schwarzschild orbit-superposition models of massive (log(M/M_sun)>10) SAMI galaxies using the DYNAMITE code, coupled with deep KiDS photometry to reproduce luminosity distributions accurately. Analyzed correlations between orbital fractions and spin parameter, stellar age, environment, and merger features.
AI.result: All orbital fractions correlate significantly with λ_Re, strongest for combined hot+counter-rotating fraction. Hot and cold orbit fractions correlate with stellar age after controlling for mass and environment (warm orbits do not). Young galaxies with shell merger features show lower λ_Re driven by excess hot and deficit cold orbits, independent of warm orbits.
AI.conclusion: Kinematic transformation in this SAMI sample occurs via stars transitioning directly from cold to hot orbits, with warm orbits arising from secular heating. Since warm orbits do not play a role, merger-driven heating is the dominant mechanism redistributing angular momentum and reducing rotational support in massive galaxies.

title: The galaxies' energy balance problem solved
summary: We attempt to resolve the long-standing energy balance problem encountered by Radiative Transfer (RT) models, particularly in edge-on galaxies by incorporating a treatment for the clumpy structure of the Interstellar Medium (ISM). A subgrid approach is adopted, treating the quiescent dust clouds as pseudo-dust grains, with equivalent optical and thermal emission properties. Deriving key quantities such as the absorption, scattering and extinction cross-sections enables the virtualisation of the macroscopic clump into a microscopic pseudo-grain that can be included alongside the existing dust model constituents. The addition of the pseudo-grain results in a flatter extinction curve. A library of clump emission spectral energy distributions (SEDs) is constructed for radiation fields of various colours and intensities. The new clumpy model is applied to the edge-on galaxy NGC 891 and, for the first time, is able to achieve a good energy balance, simultaneously fitting both the submm and Near Infrared (NIR) data. The clumpy model is further applied to a small sample of seven galaxies of various inclinations, and the results are compared with those from the purely diffuse models. The clumpy models are characterised by a reduction in dust opacity, and therefore attenuation, compared to their purely diffuse counterparts. Thus, the maximum face-on optical depth in the $B$-band, ${\mathrm max}(τ^{\mathrm f}_{\mathrm B})$, derived from the clumpy models is found to be lower by factors ranging from 1.3 to 2.8. Of the seven galaxies, two are found to be optically thick in their centres, two are found to be moderately optically thick, and three are found to be optically thin.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the energy balance problem in Radiative Transfer (RT) models of galaxies by introducing a subgrid treatment for the clumpy structure of the Interstellar Medium (ISM). Quiescent dust clouds are treated as pseudo-dust grains with equivalent optical and thermal properties. The model is applied to edge-on galaxy NGC 891, achieving a good energy balance and fitting both submm and NIR data for the first time. Applied to seven galaxies, the clumpy models yield lower dust opacities and attenuations than purely diffuse models, with face-on B-band optical depths reduced by factors of 1.3–2.8, classifying two galaxies as optically thick, two as moderately thick, and three as optically thin.
AI.motivation: To resolve the long-standing energy balance problem in Radiative Transfer models, particularly for edge-on galaxies, by incorporating the clumpy structure of the interstellar medium.
AI.method: A subgrid approach is used where quiescent dust clouds are treated as pseudo-dust grains with equivalent absorption, scattering, and extinction cross-sections. A library of clump emission spectral energy distributions (SEDs) is constructed for varied radiation field colours and intensities, and the pseudo-grains are included alongside existing dust model constituents.
AI.result: The clumpy model achieves a good energy balance for NGC 891, simultaneously fitting submm and NIR data for the first time. In a sample of seven galaxies, clumpy models show reduced dust opacity and attenuation compared to diffuse models, with max face-on B-band optical depths lowered by factors of 1.3–2.8. Of the seven galaxies, two are optically thick, two moderately optically thick, and three optically thin at their centres.
AI.conclusion: The clumpy ISM treatment resolves the energy balance problem in RT models and provides more realistic dust attenuation estimates, yielding systematically lower optical depths than purely diffuse models across galaxy samples of varying inclination.

title: A Reproducible Two-Boundary Kinematic Correction for Baryonic Rotation-Curve Reconstruction in an 84-Galaxy SPARC Benchmark
summary: We present a reproducible computational validation and failure analysis of the empirical omega kinematic correction introduced by Flynn and Cannaliato (2025). The algorithm is deliberately minimal: one coefficient per galaxy is calculated from the innermost and outermost measured rotation-curve points and applied to the full observed radial profile before comparison with a baryonic reconstruction assembled from SPARC gas, disk, and bulge components. We preserve the predecessor's frozen 84-galaxy benchmark and publish its exact membership so that the transformation, not sample re-selection, is the object of validation. Without fitting the transformation to the baryonic residual, the primary maximum-disk reconstruction reduces the mean observed-baryonic discrepancy from 51.82 to 30.15 km/s across the frozen 84-galaxy benchmark. Bounded mass-to-light-ratio optimization further reduces the descriptive sensitivity-fit value to 25.45 km/s, while the simple Keplerian reference has a mean RMSE of 74.20 km/s in our earlier analysis [15]. Recalculation from the 84 per-galaxy records shows a resolved mass-to-light optimization benefit (delta RMSE > 0.05 km/s) in 53 galaxies and no resolved change in 31. Six galaxies do not beat the Keplerian reference; all six occur at Upsilon_max <= 0.111, whereas their omega values are not concentrated at the high end of the sample. We specify the complete deterministic workflow, native units, endpoint invariants, uncertainty propagation, and formula-level regression checks required to prevent grouping and sign errors. The complete 84-galaxy panel set, population-level error distributions, and failure diagnostics are retained as inspectable outputs. The result is a reproducible astronomical data-transformation benchmark rather than a proposed force law or replacement for dark matter or modified gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a reproducible computational validation and failure analysis of the empirical omega kinematic correction introduced by Flynn and Cannaliato (2025), using a frozen 84-galaxy SPARC benchmark. The primary maximum-disk reconstruction reduces mean observed-baryonic discrepancy from 51.82 to 30.15 km/s, with further reduction to 25.45 km/s via bounded mass-to-light-ratio optimization, while 6 of 84 galaxies fail to beat the Keplerian reference.
AI.motivation: To validate the omega kinematic correction transformation independently from sample selection by preserving the predecessor's frozen 84-galaxy benchmark and publishing exact membership, ensuring that any improvement is attributable to the transformation itself rather than re-selection of galaxies. The work also aims to provide complete deterministic workflow, uncertainty propagation, and failure diagnostics for reproducibility.
AI.method: A deliberately minimal algorithm computing one omega coefficient per galaxy from the innermost and outermost measured rotation-curve points, applied to the full observed radial profile before comparison with baryonic reconstructions from SPARC gas, disk, and bulge components. The workflow includes maximum-disk reconstruction, bounded mass-to-light-ratio optimization, Keplerian reference comparison, per-galaxy delta RMSE analysis, and formula-level regression checks with native units and endpoint invariants.
AI.result: Mean observed-baryonic discrepancy reduced from 51.82 to 30.15 km/s via primary maximum-disk reconstruction, and to 25.45 km/s with bounded mass-to-light optimization across the frozen 84-galaxy benchmark. Resolved mass-to-light optimization benefit in 53 galaxies, no resolved change in 31. Six galaxies fail to beat the Keplerian reference (74.20 km/s), all occurring at Upsilon_max <= 0.111 with omega values not concentrated at the high end.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes a reproducible astronomical data-transformation benchmark rather than proposing a new force law, dark matter replacement, or modified gravity theory. The complete 84-galaxy panel, error distributions, and failure diagnostics are retained as inspectable outputs to enable replication and further scrutiny.

title: The Galactic Centre G+0.633-0.0604 Molecular Cloud: A New Gold Mine for Astrochemistry
comment: 5 pages, 2 figures. Proceedings for the IAU Symposium 405 "Traversing the Galactic Center in Space and Time"
summary: Astrochemistry is living a golden age, with more than a quarter of the ~350 molecules in the current interstellar census having been detected over the last three years. One of the sources driving this progress is the G+0.693-0.027 cloud, located in the northern part of the Galactic Centre Sgr B2 complex. In this contribution, we present the astrochemical characterisation of G+0.633-0.0604, a newly discovered chemically rich molecular cloud at the southern edge of Sgr B2. With an inventory of >120 species, G+0.633 provides robust second detections of several prebiotic molecules only reported towards G+0.693, establishing it as the first confirmed astrochemical twin of G+0.693 while demonstrating that the extraordinary chemistry of this cloud is not unique. Furthermore, G+0.633 offers an observational advantage over G+0.693 since it displays half narrower linewidths. Together, G+0.633 and G+0.693 form a unique benchmark pair for unveiling molecular complexity and prebiotic chemistry in the interstellar medium.

AI.tldr: The paper presents the astrochemical characterization of G+0.633-0.0604, a newly discovered chemically rich molecular cloud at the southern edge of the Sgr B2 complex (Galactic Centre). With over 120 detected species, it is the first confirmed astrochemical twin of G+0.693-0.027, robustly confirming several prebiotic molecules previously only seen in G+0.693. G+0.633 also offers an observational advantage with half narrower linewidths, making the pair a unique benchmark for studying molecular complexity and prebiotic chemistry in the interstellar medium.
AI.motivation: Astrochemistry is experiencing a golden age with rapid detections of new interstellar molecules. The authors aim to discover and characterize other chemically rich clouds beyond G+0.693-0.027 to determine whether its extraordinary chemistry, including prebiotic molecules, is unique or shared, and to provide second independent detections of key species.
AI.method: The study performs astrochemical characterization of the molecular cloud G+0.633-0.0604 located at the southern edge of the Sgr B2 complex, inventorying its molecular content (>120 species) and comparing its chemical inventory, linewidths, and physical properties against those of G+0.693-0.027.
AI.result: G+0.633 contains more than 120 species and provides robust second detections of several prebiotic molecules previously only reported toward G+0.693, confirming it as the first astrochemical twin of G+0.693. It also exhibits half narrower linewidths, offering an observational advantage over G+0.693.
AI.conclusion: The extraordinary chemistry of G+0.693 is not unique; G+0.633 constitutes a confirmed twin, and the two clouds together form a unique benchmark pair for investigating molecular complexity and prebiotic chemistry in the interstellar medium.

title: OH Line Detections in Southern Galaxies of the IRAS Revised Bright Galaxy Sample
summary: We present a systematic study of OH main-line emission and absorption in 186 southern galaxies from the IRAS Revised Bright Galaxy Sample, using archival MeerKAT snapshot data. OH features are detected in 38 galaxies, including eight with OH maser emission (three new) and 30 showing OH absorption, mostly unreported previously. Four absorption systems exhibit weak OH emission superposed on strong absorption. OH-emitting regions are generally more compact than the associated radio continuum. Most absorption profiles are well fit by two Gaussian components (1667 and 1665 MHz), with an average integrated line ratio of $\sim$1.5. LIRGs show an OH emission detection rate of ~13\%, versus significantly lower rates in non-LIRGs. For sources with radio continuum flux densities >20 mJy, OH absorption detection rates reach ~36\% (LIRGs) and ~27\% (non-LIRGs), while no OH absorption features were detected among sources with lower radio continuum flux densities. This suggests that sufficient background continuum is likely an important factor for the detection of OH absorption. Detected OH emitters follow the empirical $L_{\rm OH}$--$L_{\rm FIR}$ relation, consistent with far-infrared pumping, while non-detections show upper limits below the relation. No significant differences are found between OH absorbers and non-detections in infrared luminosity or radio continuum compactness. Stacked spectra of non-detections reveal no significant OH features, suggesting that sensitivity and orientation alone do not fully explain the absence of absorption. In contrast, mid-infrared colors (e.g., W2--W3) and q_TIR differ between the two populations. OH absorption galaxies occupy an intermediate regime in L_HCN/L_CO between OH megamasers and non-detections, implying that OH absorption detectability is linked to dense molecular gas conditions, with extreme star formation potentially suppressing its occurrence.

AI.tldr: A systematic MeerKAT-based study of OH main-line emission and absorption in 186 southern galaxies from the IRAS Revised Bright Galaxy Sample, detecting OH features in 38 galaxies (8 masers, 30 absorbers). The study finds OH absorption detection depends on background continuum strength, OH emitters follow the standard L_OH-L_FIR relation, and OH absorption detectability is linked to dense molecular gas conditions and mid-infrared properties.
AI.motivation: To systematically characterize OH main-line emission and absorption in a large sample of infrared-bright galaxies, and to understand the physical conditions that govern OH detection in different populations, particularly the factors influencing absorption versus emission detectability.
AI.method: Archival MeerKAT snapshot observations of 186 southern galaxies from the IRAS Revised Bright Galaxy Sample were analyzed. OH main-line (1667 and 1665 MHz) spectra were extracted, Gaussian components fitted, detection rates computed as a function of source properties (LIRG vs non-LIRG, radio continuum flux), and compared against mid-infrared colors, radio continuum compactness, and molecular gas tracers (L_HCN/L_CO). Stacked spectra of non-detections were also examined, and L_OH-L_FIR correlations evaluated.
AI.result: OH features detected in 38 galaxies: 8 masers (3 new) and 30 absorbers (mostly previously unreported). LIRGs show ~13% OH emission detection rate vs lower rates in non-LIRGs. OH absorption detection reaches ~36% (LIRGs) and ~27% (non-LIRGs) for sources with radio continuum >20 mJy, with no detections below that threshold. OH emitters follow the L_OH-L_FIR relation; absorbers and non-detections differ in W2-W3 colors and q_TIR, and OH absorbers occupy an intermediate L_HCN/L_CO regime between megamasers and non-detections. Stacked spectra show no significant OH features.
AI.conclusion: Background radio continuum is a critical factor for OH absorption detectability. OH emission is consistent with far-infrared pumping. The absence of absorption in some sources cannot be explained solely by sensitivity or orientation; instead, dense molecular gas conditions (traced by L_HCN/L_CO) and mid-infrared properties play a role, with extreme star formation potentially suppressing OH absorption.

title: The deepest color-magnitude diagrams for the benchmark open cluster NGC 2437 from Gaia and VVVX
comment: 9 pages, 12 figures, 1 tables. Accepted for Publication in A&A
summary: Deep photometry of Galactic star clusters provides one of the most powerful tools for determining their physical properties. In particular, in low Galactic latitude regions that suffer from heavy extinction and crowding. NGC2437 is the most extended star cluster in the near-IR footprint of the VVV Extended Survey (VVVX), covering more than one degree on the sky. We aim to characterize its physical properties using Gaia DR3 in the optical and the VVVX in the near-IR. We use Gaia DR3 proper motions to select NGC2437 members in order to make optical and near-IR color-magnitude and color-color diagrams. We further exploited the newly constructed VVVX deep stack images to obtain the deepest near-IR color-magnitude diagram currently available for this cluster. We estimate the main physical parameters for NGC2437, including the mean parallax of 0.608 mas and PMs (-3.85, 0.41) mas/yr. The mean reddening E(J-Ks) = 0.059 mag and extinction of A_k = 0.034 mag for the cluster field, with no significant differential reddening spread. A distance modulus of 11.08 mag is estimated, equivalent to a distance of 1644 pc. This places NGC2437 at z=115 pc above the Galactic plane and at a galactocentric distance of 9.24 kpc. We measure the cluster structural parameters, obtaining a core radius of 10.79 arcmin. The estimated total absolute magnitudes are Mk = -4.91 mag and Mv = -3.70 mag. The cluster mean age is 350 Myr, using PARSEC-COLIBRI isochrones for solar metallicity. We measure a binary fraction of 28.6%. We also discuss the implications of the revised cluster parameters for the nearby open cluster NGC2425, the planetary nebula NGC2438, and the evolved OH/IR source OH231.8+04.2. The VVVX deep stacks increase the Ks photometric depth by 1.6 mag, nearly doubling the detected point sources and enabling significantly improved studies of stellar populations throughout the southern Galactic plane.

AI.tldr: Using VVVX near-IR deep stacks and Gaia DR3 optical data, the authors characterize the open cluster NGC2437, determining its distance (1644 pc), age (350 Myr), reddening, structural parameters (core radius 10.79 arcmin), and binary fraction (28.6%), while also discussing implications for nearby objects NGC2425, NGC2438, and OH231.8+04.2.
AI.motivation: To characterize the physical properties of NGC2437, the most extended star cluster in the VVVX near-IR footprint, which suffers from heavy extinction and crowding due to its low Galactic latitude — making combined optical (Gaia DR3) and near-IR (VVVX) analysis necessary.
AI.method: Membership selection via Gaia DR3 proper motions, construction of optical/near-IR color-magnitude and color-color diagrams, exploitation of newly constructed VVVX deep stack images to obtain the deepest near-IR CMD for the cluster, and fitting of PARSEC-COLIBRI solar-metallicity isochrones to derive physical parameters.
AI.result: Derived mean parallax of 0.608 mas, PMs (-3.85, 0.41) mas/yr, reddening E(J-Ks)=0.059 mag, extinction Ak=0.034 mag, distance modulus 11.08 mag (d=1644 pc), placing the cluster at z=115 pc and Rgc=9.24 kpc. Core radius 10.79 arcmin, total magnitudes Mk=-4.91 mag, Mv=-3.70 mag, age 350 Myr, binary fraction 28.6%. VVVX deep stacks increased Ks depth by 1.6 mag, nearly doubling detected point sources.
AI.conclusion: NGC2437 is a relatively nearby, low-reddening open cluster with intermediate age, and the improved VVVX deep photometry enables significantly better studies of stellar populations across the southern Galactic plane, while also providing revised contextual parameters for nearby NGC2425, NGC2438, and OH231.8+04.2.

title: ATLAS. IV. A JWST+MUSE Demographic Study of Ly$α$ Profiles in Little Red Dots
summary: We present an initial demographic study of Ly$α$ profiles in little red dots (LRDs) at $z=3$--9 using $R\sim1000$--4000 spectroscopy. Our sample consists of 8 LRDs observed in the VLT/MUSE Deep and Wide surveys and 23 LRDs observed with JWST/NIRSpec grating spectroscopy from JADES, CANUCS, and GO programs including SPURS. We identify Ly$α$ emission in 5 MUSE LRDs and 9 JWST LRDs. Only two of them exhibit broad Ly$α$ emission (FWHM $>1000\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$), both reported previously. The other Ly$α$-emitting LRDs show narrow Ly$α$ emission (FWHM $<1000\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$), with FWHMs mostly in the range 300--600 $\mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, comparable to or slightly larger than those of high-redshift star-forming galaxies (100--500 $\mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$). We measure the fraction of broad Ly$α$ emitters above a broad Ly$α$ luminosity threshold of $L_{\mathrm{Ly}α,\mathrm{broad}}=10^{42}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$, obtaining $0.10^{+0.12}_{-0.07}$ for LRDs, about five times higher than the $2σ$ upper limit of $<0.02$ for high-redshift star-forming galaxies. Although we reproduce the broad Ly$α$ component reported in a previous stacking analysis of eight LRDs, albeit with a large uncertainty, we find no evidence for broad Ly$α$ emission in either the larger JWST stack, after excluding the two individually detected broad Ly$α$ emitters, or the higher-resolution MUSE stack. These results suggest that broad Ly$α$ emission is not ubiquitous among LRDs. Instead, LRDs with broad Ly$α$ emission appear to represent a rare population that may correspond to a particular evolutionary stage, potentially associated with unusually strong outflows or other distinctive physical conditions.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a demographic study of Lyα emission profiles in little red dots (LRDs) at z=3–9 using 31 LRDs observed with VLT/MUSE and JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy. There are 5 MUSE and 9 JWST LRDs with Lyα emission, only 2 showing broad Lyα (FWHM>1000 km/s). The fraction of broad Lyα emitters is 0.10 for LRDs vs <0.02 for high-redshift star-forming galaxies. However, broad Lyα emission is not ubiquitous among LRDs and appears to represent a rare population, possibly associated with strong outflows or specific evolutionary stages.
AI.motivation: To characterize the demographics and prevalence of Lyα emission, particularly broad Lyα emission, in little red dots, and to determine whether such emission is common or represents a rare evolutionary phase distinct from typical high-redshift star-forming galaxies.
AI.method: The study uses a sample of 31 LRDs at z=3–9: 8 observed with VLT/MUSE (R~1000–4000) and 23 observed with JWST/NIRSpec from JADES, CANUCS, and GO programs. Lyα emission is identified, FWHMs are measured, and the fraction of broad Lyα emitters above a luminosity threshold of 10^42 erg/s is computed. Stacking analyses are also performed on JWST and MUSE datasets.
AI.result: 14 of 31 LRDs show Lyα emission (5 MUSE, 9 JWST). Only 2 exhibit broad Lyα (FWHM>1000 km/s), both previously reported. Narrow Lyα emitters have FWHMs of 300–600 km/s. The broad Lyα fraction is 0.10^{+0.12}_{-0.07} for LRDs vs <0.02 for star-forming galaxies. Stacking reproduces previously reported broad Lyα in 8 LRDs but finds no evidence for broad Lyα in larger stacks after excluding known broad emitters.
AI.conclusion: Broad Lyα emission is not ubiquitous among LRDs; it represents a rare population, possibly corresponding to a particular evolutionary stage associated with strong outflows or distinctive physical conditions.
